links.outcome: Bias in sleep-scoring derived markers across demographic and clinical factors such as age
links.effect: Identified biases such as age-related shifts in U-Sleep and YASA predictions, though both maintained non-inferior performance in sleep apnea risk assessment. No numbers reported in abstract.
links.quote: Applying it to the widely recognized U-Sleep and YASA sleep-scoring algorithms, we identify biases—such as age-related shifts—indicating missing input information or imbalances in training data.

unlisted_practices: Distribution-based (quantile) analysis of how external factors shape predictive errors, extending Bland-Altman validation

screen.reason: The authors propose and empirically demonstrate a validation framework to evaluate algorithmic bias and performance distributions across demographics (e.g. age) for automated sleep scoring algorithms (U-Sleep and YASA).

primary.practice: algorithmic bias and distributional performance evaluation framework
